h: What is an AI agent with a wallet?
s: Software that can sign transactions for you. Useful, and risky without limits.
cap: An AI agent with a wallet is software that can sign transactions on your behalf. Useful, and risky without limits. AegisNet gives it a name (ENS), clean routes (1inch, Uniswap v4) and a human veto (World ID).

h: Why give an agent a name?
s: A readable identity beats a raw address. AegisNet binds every agent to an ENS identity.
cap: Why give an agent a name? A readable identity beats a raw address, and it makes an agent easier to recognise and track. AegisNet binds every agent to an ENS identity, like agent1.aegisnet.eth.

s: A way to show a real person stands behind an approval. AegisNet pauses high-value moves for World ID proof of human.
cap: Proof of human: a way to show that a real person stands behind an approval. AegisNet pauses high-value moves for World ID proof of human, so agents act and humans keep the veto.

s: The path a trade takes to find a price. AegisNet routes trades through 1inch SwapVM and Uniswap v4.
cap: A swap route is the path a trade takes to find its price. AegisNet routes an agent's trades through 1inch SwapVM and Uniswap v4: clean routes instead of ad hoc ones.

s: Small ones run. Big ones wait. Rogue ones stop.
cap: Every trade, three outcomes. Small ones run. Big ones wait for a human. Rogue ones stop. That's the design: routine to auto, big calls to you.

s: The AegisNet site walks through three situations an agent can face.
cap: Three situations, walked through on the AegisNet site. See how an agent's trades are handled, and where a human steps in. Building on Sepolia testnet. aegisnet.solrun.fun

s: A request traced through four phases, shown on the AegisNet site.
cap: Four phases, one request. The AegisNet site traces how a request moves from an agent to a trade, so you can see where each check sits. Testnet only.

s: The dashboard on aegisnet.solrun.fun. Testnet.
cap: Your AI agent's control room: the AegisNet dashboard, where an owner sets the guardrails and watches what the agent does. Building on Sepolia testnet.

s: A guided walkthrough on the AegisNet site.
cap: Five steps, in order: the walkthrough on the AegisNet site takes you from connecting a wallet to guarded trades. Testnet. aegisnet.solrun.fun

h: Big calls go to a human.
s: From $1,000, a move passes the Midnight ZK gate and waits for World ID proof of human.
cap: Big calls go to a human. On the AegisNet site, a move of $1,000 or more passes the Midnight ZK gate and waits for World ID proof of human before it clears. Testnet.

s: AegisNet is building on Sepolia testnet. The site lists five contracts live there.
cap: AegisNet is building on Sepolia testnet. The site lists five contracts live there: a place to see how the pieces fit before anything touches mainnet. Testnet only.

h: How much would you let an agent move alone?
s: Reply with A, B, C or D.
cap: Community question: how much would you let an AI agent move without asking you? A) Nothing B) Up to $100 C) Up to $1,000 D) More, with clear limits. Tell us your reasoning.

h: What should an agent never do alone?
items: D  Buy a brand new token
s: Reply with A, B, C or D.
cap: What should an AI agent never do alone? A) Move large sums B) Approve new contracts C) Change its own limits D) Buy a brand new token. Your answers shape how we think about guardrails.

h: What would you name your agent?
s: Reply with your best ENS-style name.
cap: Every agent on AegisNet gets an ENS identity, like agent1.aegisnet.eth. What would you name yours? Reply with your best ENS-style name.

s: Our view.
cap: Our view: autonomy needs a brake pedal. An AI agent with your wallet and no brakes is a liability. Give it limits, and a human who can say no.

h: The best approval is the one you only see when it matters.
s: Our view.
cap: Our view: the best approval is the one you only see when it matters. Routine should run on its own; the big calls should come to you.

s: Hypothetical. Small trades run on their own. A large one waits for a human.
cap: Use case (hypothetical): a treasury agent rebalances a portfolio. The routine trades run on their own; a large one waits for a human to clear it. Illustration only, on testnet.

s: Hypothetical. Try the guardrails with testnet funds before anything real is at stake.
cap: Use case (hypothetical): try an agent on Sepolia testnet first. Watch the routes, the identity and the veto work with testnet funds before real money is anywhere near.

s: AegisNet is building on Sepolia testnet. Everything shown is testnet.
cap: We're early. AegisNet is building on Sepolia testnet, so everything you see is testnet. Agents act, humans keep the veto, and we're building it in the open.

s: Let AI agents trade onchain, with a human on the big calls.
cap: AegisNet: let AI agents trade onchain, with a human on the big calls. Every agent gets an ENS identity, clean routes through 1inch and Uniswap v4, and a World ID human veto. Building on Sepolia testnet. aegisnet.solrun.fun
